title: References vs pointers
summary: A reference is another name. A pointer is its own variable.

cards.title: Nicknames
cards.body: If your friend Robert is also called Rob, there is still only **one** person. A **reference** works the same: `int& ref = hp;` gives hp a second name. No new box is created.
Notice the cell labelled `hp / ref`: one box, two names. The pointer gets its own box.

cards.title: When to use which
cards.body:
- A **reference** must be set when it is created, can't be null, and can't be re-pointed. Use it by default for "I need access to that object".
- A **pointer** can be `nullptr` ("nothing"), and can be changed to point elsewhere. Use it when "maybe nothing" or "changes target" is part of the meaning.
- `const Player& p` is the standard way to pass a big object you only read: no copy, no changes.

cards.question: What does this print?
cards.explain: r is another name for x. Assigning to r assigns to x.

cards.question: Which of these can legally be null?
cards.explain: A pointer can hold `nullptr`. A reference must always refer to a real object.
